product: Gas turbines: 2026-07-22 Q2 booked 20 GW new gas equipment contracts, including 52 heavy-duty units with 15 HA turbines, plus grid equipment such as switchgear, transformers and HVDC, and services. The demand driver is AI data centers and electrification; data-center orders exceeded 5B year-to-date (2026-07-22). Nuclear BWRX-300 SMR adds longer-dated demand (Sweden 2026-09-03, Europe MoU 2026-09-22).
demand: Both. 2026-07-22: Power orders up 134 pct on higher gas volume and price; Electrification revenue up 68 pct, 29 pct organic, on switchgear and transformer volume; adjusted EBITDA margin up 280 bps to 11.3 pct on volume, price and productivity. Price leads in gas, volume in grid. Wind is volume loss, organic revenue down 11 pct (2026-07-22).
pricing_power: Wind is acute: 2026-07-22 Q2 Wind segment EBITDA was -275M, margin -13.6 pct, FY26 guided to about -400M on offshore project cost overruns. Other risks: inflation and tariffs on fixed-price long-cycle contracts, slot reservations failing to convert to orders, and an AI data-center financing air pocket (Oracle and Blue Owl delay reported 2026-09-24, aggregator).
competition: Chinese suppliers are the substitutes: Shanghai Electric, Dongfang and Harbin for gas turbines; Goldwind, Envision and Mingyang for wind; Chinese transformer and HVDC makers for grid. They are cheaper but not yet qualified or permitted for large HA-class turbines in Western markets, so near-term substitution for GEV flagship gas is limited. Qualification dates not found.

bull: Q2 2026 (2026-07-22): orders 24.2B up 88% organic, backlog 176B, gas slots 100 to 116 GW, data-center orders >5B YTD, FY26 guidance raised to 45.5-46.5B revenue and 11.5-12.5B FCF.

falsifier: At the 2026-10-28 Q3 print, gas equipment under contract fails to progress toward at least 125 GW by year-end 2026, or FY26 revenue 45.5-46.5B / FCF 11.5-12.5B guidance is cut.
